chapter: Clubs, readers and musicians he knew
title: The Music Box jitney dance at Carondelet and Canal
summary: He worked a couple of weeks at the Music Box, a continuous jitney dance, replacing Arnold Metoyer.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you ever play at the place called the Music Box?
Oh wait, let's see, where was that located? Caronelet and Canal.

Yeah, I worked there a couple of weeks, it got too tough for me, because you had to continue, play continuously, you couldn't stop. You know, the, yeah, just like when I go to the sort of a Jitney style stuff. You paid for a dance and you couldn't stop, you'd take no rest. In other words, the way we'd done, we left the horns, play one chorus, and the balance of the instruments played the other chorus. Now people that were playing piano, they could play, you know, any time, all the time, because it wasn't so hard. But anybody who was playing the horns, clarinet, trumpets and stuff, you had to get a little rest. Yeah.
Yeah, I worked over there. What band was that with?
Well I didn't, there wasn't no band. I see. I was just, the Philly and the Blaze over there.
At the Crownlep Canal. Uh huh.
That's in the 20's? I don't know, I couldn't say.

It's hard to remember years. I couldn't remember. But uh, the man who, I think, had this job, was his original job, I think it was this fellow, Matwyer, Arnold Matwyer. Oh. I think he was the man with his, that was his job. When you took his place? I took his place for a couple of weeks. Oh I see.
Well he used to leave town. Yeah.
He was on the play with Sir Hicks.
